[L1158] 6. SUBSTANCES
[L1159] Alcohol. Functional, persistent, solo. Onset of the pattern is observable in the late Directorship
[L1160] era and is established by the Osborn arc. Modal beverage: brown liquor (bourbon or rye), neat,
[L1161] two to three pours across an evening, on perhaps four nights of seven. She does not drink to
[L1162] intoxication on operational nights. She does not drink in company except ceremonially. The
[L1163] function is sleep onset, cortisol blunting, and the closure of the day's open files in her head —
[L1164] not socialization, not pleasure. Tolerance is moderate-to-high. She has never sought help; she
[L1165] would not. Categorize as mild Alcohol Use Disorder, occupational, watch item rather than crisis.
[L1166] Caffeine. Heavy. Coffee from waking through late afternoon; black, no sugar. Approximate daily
[L1167] intake 400–600 mg. This is the lower partner in a stimulant-depressant cycle she runs against
[L1168] her own circadian disruption.
[L1169] Nicotine. Not in evidence. If she smoked in the Army she has long since dropped it; her
[L1170] cardiovascular numbers and the absence of dental staining are consistent.
[L1171] Prescription medications. The extended-cycle oral contraceptive noted above. No on-record
[L1172] psychotropics — neither SSRI nor benzodiazepine nor sleep aid, which is itself a behavioral
[L1173] choice: she would meet criteria for an evening anxiolytic or a short-course sleep agent, and she
[L1174] will not request either, because the request would enter a file. Occasional NSAIDs for the
[L1175] lumbar and the right shoulder. Standard field medkit access (the operator's pharmacy) including
[L1176] stimulants for sustained operations — used sparingly, reportedly, and only when the mission
[L1177] frames it.
[L1178] Illicit substances. None in evidence, none consistent with her risk profile.
[L1179] 7. SLEEP, CIRCADIAN, AND METABOLIC
[L1180] Thigh: left lateral — paired scars (entry/exit) from the through-and-through GSW; deep￾tissue adhesion palpable.
[L1181] Knees: right — minor surface scarring from falls.
[L1182] Head, central forehead: the entrance wound from the execution. Whether it is visible on
[L1183] the restored body depends on the resurrection modality; behaviorally, she does not check
[L1184] for it in mirrors.[L1185] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 38 / 206>[L1186] Sleep architecture. Fragmented, short, weapon-adjacent. Average total sleep 5.0–5.5 hours,
[L1187] taken in two segments (a longer block of perhaps 3.5–4 hours and a secondary nap of 60–90
[L1188] minutes when operationally permitted). Onset latency under 10 minutes when alcohol-assisted;
[L1189] 30+ minutes without. Wake events multiple per night, brief, oriented (she wakes oriented to her
[L1190] sidearm and the door). REM percentage almost certainly suppressed by the alcohol pattern,
[L1191] which has subtle but real effects on emotional memory consolidation — relevant to her capacity
[L1192] to carry secret-knowledge load without daytime intrusion.
[L1193] Circadian. No stable phase. The Helicarrier is her residence; the lighting is artificial; the
[L1194] operational tempo dictates her clock. She has not slept in true darkness, on a non-pressurized
[L1195] surface, for a contiguous week, in years.
[L1196] Nutrition. Adequate, monitored, joyless. Mess intake; protein-forward; carbohydrate restricted
[L1197] at her own discretion; she eats standing, walking, or at her desk. She does not cook. She does
[L1198] not remember the last meal she ate slowly.
[L1199] Metabolic markers (projected). Lipids well-controlled by exertion and diet; fasting glucose
[L1200] normal; hsCRP probably elevated owing to chronic stress load; cortisol curve flattened (high
[L1201] evening, sluggish morning rise) — the endocrine fingerprint of a senior intelligence officer in her
[L1202] tenure window.
[L1203] 8. NEUROLOGICAL AND COGNITIVE
[L1204] Head injury burden. Aggregate of one in-service concussion, multiple unreported subclinical
[L1205] events, two Helicarrier-era blast exposures, and a fatal GSW to the head from which she has
[L1206] been restored. Even discounting the execution as medically discontinuous, the antecedent load
[L1207] is consistent with low-grade chronic traumatic exposure. Subjective symptoms she would not
[L1208] report: occasional word-finding pauses she covers with deliberate cadence; a slightly slowed
[L1209] dark-adaptation; mild migraine-spectrum headaches in the late afternoon, frontotemporal,
[L1210] bilateral.
[L1211] Cognitive function. Working memory remains exceptional — the operational evidence is
[L1212] unambiguous. Executive function intact; threat assessment fast and accurate; pattern
[L1213] recognition strong. The compression effect of chronic stress on long-horizon memory
[L1214] consolidation is real but compensated by procedural rigor (she takes notes; she keeps logs; she
[L1215] does not trust her recall the way she did at 28, and she has adapted).
[L1216] Pain. Chronic low-grade lumbar; intermittent right shoulder; old thigh wound aches on long sits.
[L1217] She does not name pain when asked. She integrates it.[L1218] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 39 / 206>[L1219] 9. PSYCHOLOGICAL IMPACT — SOMATIC SUBSTRATE
[L1220] Each injury entry above has a psychological residue. Mapped explicitly:
[L1221] She has been shot, blown up, hunted, executed, and restored. She has carried planet-ending
[L1222] knowledge in a body kept upright by coffee, bourbon, and the architecture of a job that flatters
[L1223] her damage by calling it duty. The medical record is exhaustive; the prognosis is stable until it
[L1224] isn't; and there is no provider on the manifest she would let close enough to change that.

[L1228] SOMATIC ATLAS — SUBJECT: HILL, MARIA (CMDR.)
[L1229] Body-level intelligence compile. Every observable physical signature, longitudinally mapped,
[L1230] with state-dependent variance. Surveillance-grade granularity; nothing here is decorative —

[L1232] I. BASELINE ANTHROPOMETRY & STANDING FRAME
[L1233] The first time she pointed a Helicarrier gun at Captain America was not somatically
[L1234] traumatic. It was somatically confirming — the body learned that procedure could be
[L1235] deployed under maximum interpersonal cost and survive. The lesson stuck.
[L1236] The first time she drew on Stark and did not fire was somatically formative. The
[L1237] hesitation cost her something; she has not let herself hesitate the same way since, and she
[L1238] has also not let herself fire on a friend since. Both adaptations live in the same nervous
[L1239] system.
[L1240] The Osborn-era GSWs taught her body that the institution would not catch her. The
[L1241] hypervigilance baseline dates from here and has not reset.
[L1242] The Illuminati knowledge load did not produce a discrete trauma; it produced a slow
[L1243] grinding of the affect regulation system, observable as the dysthymic baseline and the
[L1244] alcohol pattern. This is the most medically important thing about her and the least visible.
[L1245] The execution is the unmetabolized event. There is no behavioral evidence that she has
[L1246] processed it. There is behavioral evidence that she has narrowed around it: tighter circle,
[L1247] harder compartmentalization, a marginally faster draw, and a refusal to be alone in a room
[L1248] with anyone wearing the wrong uniform.[L1249] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 40 / 206>[L1250] Five-foot-nine in boots, five-seven without. Frame is long-muscled rather than bulked — the
[L1251] build of a runner who lifts to standard, not of someone who trains for show. Resting weight
[L1252] holds in a tight band; under operational load it drops three to five pounds and does not come
[L1253] back until the op closes. Shoulders square and pulled fractionally back at all times — not the
[L1254] rigid brace of parade-ground posture but the loaded readiness of someone who has been
[L1255] knocked down enough times to keep her center of mass forward of her heels.
[L1256] She stands with weight ninety-percent on the strong-side leg (left), strong-side hip cocked
[L1257] maybe two degrees, weak-side foot angled fifteen degrees outboard. This is a draw-stance held
[L1258] permanently — she can clear leather from this position without telegraphing a weight shift.
[L1259] People who train with her notice within a week; people who don't, never do. In dress uniform
[L1260] standing at attention she breaks this and goes textbook symmetrical, which reads, to anyone
[L1261] who knows her, as a kind of costume.
[L1262] Hands rest at the seam in formal contexts; in field gear they rest at the duty belt, dominant
[L1263] thumb hooked behind the magazine pouches, off-hand loose. Arms cross only when she is
[L1264] cold, never when she is defensive — defensive Hill keeps her hands free.
[L1265] II. GAIT, MOVEMENT, ROOM-USE
[L1266] Walking gait. Step length 28–30 inches at office cadence, shortening to 24 inches in corridors
[L1267] she considers tactical. Heel-strike is quiet — she has trained the strike out of her boots, lands
[L1268] midfoot on hard surfaces, and the sound of her approach is signature-low. Subordinates report
[L1269] not hearing her until she is at the door; this is not deliberate stealth but a residue of a decade of
[L1270] moving through environments where being heard meant being a target.
[L1271] Cadence. Steady, metronomic, unchanging across distances. She does not speed up when
[L1272] late and does not slow down when tired. The metronome breaks only under two conditions:
[L1273] pursuit (where she lengthens stride markedly and the heel-strike returns), and the corridor
[L1274] outside an Illuminati or directorate meeting she does not want to enter, where her cadence
[L1275] drops by perhaps fifteen percent for the last twenty feet.
[L1276] Room entry. Enters every room with a sub-second left-to-right sweep — corners first, then
[L1277] exits, then occupants by threat-ranking, then friendlies. The sweep is so habituated that it
[L1278] occurs in conference rooms she has used a thousand times. She will not sit with her back to a
[L1279] door. In rooms with no compliant seat she stands. In rooms where the only compliant seat is the
[L1280] head of the table she takes it without comment and people read it as authority; it is not.
[L1281] Stair behavior. Down: rapid, controlled, hand never on the rail unless carrying. Up: same
[L1282] speed regardless of flights — pace does not degrade through five flights of Helicarrier stairs,
[L1283] which is a real cardiovascular signature.[L1284] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 41 / 206>[L1285] Vehicle behavior. Drives left-hand on the wheel, right resting on the gear-shift or thigh near
[L1286] sidearm. In passenger configuration she sits behind the driver (best sightline, best draw angle
[L1287] on a hostile driver). Will not sit in the front passenger seat unless someone she trusts
[L1288] operationally is driving — Fury, Stark post-extraction, Rogers. The list is short.
[L1289] III. FACIAL ARCHITECTURE & MICROEXPRESSION
[L1290] Resting face. Mouth a flat horizontal, corners neither up nor down — a deliberate
[L1291] neutralization, not natural slackness. Jaw set so that the masseter is faintly visible under the
[L1292] skin even at rest; jaw-clench is her default tonic state and dentition shows the wear (she grinds
[L1293] in sleep — see §VII).
[L1294] The eyes are the most legible thing about her and she knows it; she compensates by reducing
[L1295] blink rate under scrutiny (down to eight-to-ten per minute against a baseline of fifteen) and by
[L1296] holding gaze a beat longer than civilians find comfortable. Pupils track wide and fast —
[L1297] peripheral acquisition is excellent. She has a "scan" that registers as a half-second pause mid￾conversation where her focal point drifts past the interlocutor's shoulder; this is not dissociation,
[L1298] it is a re-sweep of the room.
[L1299] Microexpressions catalogued by state:
[L1300] Calm / baseline. Brow neutral. Lip-corner symmetry. The faint micro-pull at the right corner
[L1301] of the mouth that is her version of acknowledgment — not a smile, a half-millimeter shift
[L1302] visible only on high-resolution capture.
[L1303] Mild amusement (rare, usually directed at Stark's flippancy or Fury's understatement). The
[L1304] right-corner pull deepens; brow remains still. She does not laugh on panel and does not
[L1305] laugh in life except, perhaps, alone. The exhalation through the nose — short, single — is
[L1306] her substitute.
[L1307] Annoyance. A flick of the lower lip pulled briefly inward, then released. Brow remains still —
[L1308] this is the tell that distinguishes her annoyance from anger.
[L1309] Pressure / cornered procedurally. Jaw visibly sets; she rolls the shoulders fractionally back;
[L1310] the chin lifts by perhaps two degrees. The voice flattens before the face does.
[L1311] Genuine anger. Color leaves the face rather than entering it — vasoconstriction not
[L1312] vasodilation. The blink rate drops near zero. The right hand goes still on whatever surface it
[L1313] is touching. This is the moment to disengage; everyone who has stayed past it has
[L1314] regretted it.
[L1315] Fear. Catalogued only in the Osborn arc (Invincible Iron Man extraction sequences) and the
[L1316] moments before her execution (Secret Empire #10). Manifests as a tightening at the orbital
[L1317] — the skin around the eye contracts a half-millimeter, the lid lowers a degree — and a sub-[L1318] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 42 / 206>[L1319] Smile. Asymmetric, right-side dominant, present perhaps a dozen times across the entire
[L1320] published record and never in front of more than two people. The smile reaches the eyes only
[L1321] with Fury, and only when he is being most himself.
[L1322] IV. HANDS, GESTURE, AND MICRO-MOVEMENT
[L1323] Hands are short-nailed (cut, not filed; trimmed at the desk with a service-issue clipper),
[L1324] unpolished, calluses at the thenar (pistol grip) and along the proximal interphalangeals of the
[L1325] index and middle (rifle, repeated dry-fire). Knuckles abraded faintly along the third and fourth
[L1326] metacarpals of the right hand — the residue of a habit of striking hard objects in private when
[L1327] the day has been bad. The abrasion is never fresh enough to comment on, never absent.
[L1328] Gesture vocabulary, ranked by frequency:
[L1329] audible inhale held a beat too long. She does not show fear in the face; she shows it in the
[L1330] breath.
[L1331] Grief. Almost unwitnessed. Funeral and casualty contexts: the corners of the mouth pull
[L1332] faintly down for a fraction of a second and the eyes close — not blink, close — for perhaps
[L1333] three-quarters of a second. Then re-open. Then proceed.
[L1334] Tenderness. Functionally absent in public. Inferred, from the way she stood near Fury's
[L1335] bedside on the bad night and the way she lays a hand on a subordinate's casket lid before
[L1336] the lid goes down — pressure, two seconds, withdraw. She does not stroke. She does not
[L1337] linger.
[L1338] 1. The folder-tap. Index finger of the dominant hand taps a closed folder, dataslate, or table
[L1339] edge once — a single percussive beat — when she has decided something and is about to
[L1340] issue an order. The tap precedes the verbal directive by perhaps half a second.
[L1341] Subordinates who have learned to read it begin executing on the tap.
[L1342] 2. The bridge. Both hands brought to the bridge of the nose, thumb and index of the dominant
[L1343] hand pinching at the medial canthi, eyes closed for a count of two. This is her only public
[L1344] concession to fatigue. It appears in Hickman-era Avengers debriefs with measurable
[L1345] frequency — once per Illuminati meeting, on average.
[L1346] 3. The earpiece-check. Right hand to right ear, two fingers, a quarter-second contact. This is
[L1347] reflexive even when she is not wearing an earpiece — a phantom gesture from years of
[L1348] running an op while standing in a meeting.
[L1349] 4. The holster confirm. Dominant hand brushes the grip of the sidearm during transitions
[L1350] through doors, never with conscious awareness. Confirmation that the weapon is where she
[L1351] expects it. Frequency: every door, every time.[L1352] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 43 / 206>[L1353] Gestures she does not do. She does not point at people. She does not gesture while
[L1354] speaking on the phone. She does not cross her arms in argument. She does not touch her own
[L1355] face except for the bridge and the hair-tuck. She does not fidget — no pen-clicking, no leg￾bounce, no ring-twisting (no ring). Stillness is the dominant cue and movement is therefore
[L1356] signal.
[L1357] V. VOICE, BREATH, VOCAL SOMATICS
[L1358] Pitch. Low-alto, deliberately seated lower than her natural range — she has trained the voice
[L1359] down to operate in male-dominated command environments. Under fatigue the trained register
[L1360] slips and the natural pitch surfaces, a half-octave higher; this is one of the few somatic tells that
[L1361] reads to outsiders.
[L1362] Pace. Steady at 140 words per minute in baseline command speech, dropping to 100–110
[L1363] under stress (clipped, single-clause sentences), accelerating to 170+ only when reading
[L1364] coordinates or a target list — operational data is delivered at the speed the listener can copy.
[L1365] Breath. Diaphragmatic by training. Resting respiration low and slow, twelve per minute or
[L1366] under. Under stress she lengthens the exhale rather than the inhale — combat breathing, four
[L1367] in, six out, learned at Benning and never unlearned. In genuine fear she holds the inhale a beat
[L1368] too long (see §III) which is the only somatic distinction between her stress and her terror.
[L1369] Laugh. A single short nasal exhale, mouth closed. Audible in rooms with fewer than four
[L1370] people. Never recorded in groups.
[L1371] Silences. Tactical. She uses silence the way most operators use words — to compel
[L1372] disclosure, to mark disapproval, to refuse an off-ramp from a question she has asked. The
[L1373] silence is held with steady eye contact and no facial movement. People talk into it.
[L1374] VI. GROOMING, KIT, AND BODY MAINTENANCE
[L1375] 5. The collar-straighten. Off-hand pulls the tactical collar a quarter-inch downward at the
[L1376] throat, generally after a confrontation closes — a re-composure gesture, signature,
[L1377] identifiable across decades of canon.
[L1378] 6. The hair-tuck. Right side only — she tucks the right-temple lock behind the right ear with the
[L1379] middle finger of the right hand, never the index. The off-side hair she leaves. This is the
[L1380] closest thing she has to a self-soothe and it appears under cognitive load (reading a report
[L1381] she does not like) rather than emotional load.[L1382] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 44 / 206>[L1383] Hair. Brunette, shoulder-length, cut every six weeks by the same enlisted barber aboard the
[L1384] Helicarrier — she will not use civilian salons (security and time-cost both). Worn down off-duty,
[L1385] half-up in tactical rigging, full ponytail in field deployment with the tail short enough not to grab.
[L1386] Never colored. The single gray strand at the right temple has been present in canon since the

[L1388] Skin. Unpracticed at care. SHIELD-issue moisturizer at most. The skin shows the work —

[L1392] Cosmetics. Functional. Concealer for the under-eyes when she will be on a press feed.

[L1394] Nails. As noted — short, clean, unvarnished. Never bitten (this is important; the OCPD picture

[L1397] Scent. Soap (SHIELD-issue, mild), gun oil, the faint metallic edge of body-armor liner. No

[L1400] Wardrobe. Three working configurations: tactical command kit (dominant, ~80% of waking
[L1401] hours), service dress (~15%, formal directorate functions), and a tight civilian rotation of dark

[L1405] Sidearm. Always present off-duty as well as on. In civilian clothes, holstered at the appendix for
[L1406] concealment, never small-of-back (slow draw, bad in a vehicle). Spare magazine in the left

[L1408] ankle in field configuration.
[L1409] VII. SLEEP ARCHITECTURE
[L1410] Quarters are aboard the Helicarrier — a single bunk room, regulation, undecorated except for
[L1411] one framed photograph (face-down on the desk, contents unverified, likely her brother). She
[L1412] does not maintain a civilian residence she sleeps in with any regularity.
[L1413] Sleep schedule. Bimodal. Operational nights: she stays up the duration of the op, sleeps three
[L1414] to four hours after, wakes hard, resumes. Non-operational nights: lights out around 0100, alarm[L1415] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 45 / 206>[L1416] at 0530, four-and-a-half hours, taken in one block. She does not nap. She cannot nap — the
[L1417] hypervigilance bleeds through and she will be awake in fifteen minutes.
[L1418] Sleep onset. Slow. Twenty to thirty-five minutes from horizontal to actual sleep, longer on
[L1419] nights following moral injuries (a lie told to Rogers; a teammate's memory wiped; a directive
[L1420] signed). She drinks during this window — see §IX — which lengthens onset slightly and
[L1421] degrades sleep architecture more than she registers.
[L1422] Sleep posture. Right-side, knees drawn slightly up, dominant hand under the pillow over the
[L1423] sidearm she keeps there. She will not sleep on her back (vulnerability) and rarely on her front
[L1424] (slow draw). Subordinate medics who have ever had to wake her have learned to announce
[L1425] themselves verbally from outside the doorway because reaching her while she is asleep
[L1426] produces a reliable defensive response.
[L1427] Sleep behavior. She grinds her teeth — confirmed by the molar wear pattern. She talks once
[L1428] or twice a year, sub-articulate. She does not dream report. She wakes once or twice per night to
[L1429] scan the room, registers all-clear, returns to sleep within ninety seconds. The wake-scans do
[L1430] not register to her in the morning as wakings.
[L1431] Morning ritual. Twelve to fourteen minutes, repeatable to the minute. Sit up, water (250 ml
[L1432] from the bedside flask), the bridge (§IV) for a count of five, stand, shower three minutes hot two
[L1433] minutes cold, dress (kit pre-laid the night before in a sequence that has not changed in eight
[L1434] years), holster, hair, comm-check, door. No coffee in quarters — she takes it in the command
[L1435] deck galley, two cups, black, no food until eleven.
[L1436] VIII. EATING
[L1437] Pattern. Two meals plus tactical snacking. First meal between 1100 and 1300 — whatever the
[L1438] galley is serving, eaten standing at the counter or carried back to the desk, fork in left hand
[L1439] European-style (Army habit), eyes on the dataslate. Second meal between 2000 and 2200,
[L1440] similar. She does not eat breakfast. She does not eat at table with company except under
[L1441] directorate-function obligation.
[L1442] Preferences. Strongly proteinous, carbohydrate-moderate, salt-tolerant. She will eat anything
[L1443] operational requirements present and complains about none of it. Off-duty she has been
[L1444] observed to order the same thing — grilled chicken, rice, green vegetable — from the same
[L1445] three or four restaurants near three or four safehouses. She does not experiment with food.
[L1446] Food is fuel and the menu is a solved problem.
[L1447] Speed. Fast. A meal is twelve to fifteen minutes including walk-time. She has not lingered over
[L1448] a meal on panel in published canon. The one observed exception is a sequence with Fury post-[L1449] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 46 / 206>[L1450] Secret Invasion — bar food, two hours, the longest meal of her life and possibly the most
[L1451] important.
[L1452] Water. Consistent. She carries a bottle and refills it. Hydration is a discipline.
[L1453] What she will not eat in company. Anything that requires fingers. Anything that risks staining
[L1454] the kit. Anything she would have to look at to manage. She eats with her hands free and her
[L1455] sightlines clear.
[L1456] IX. SUBSTANCE INGESTION
[L1457] Caffeine. Two cups black coffee on rising, one mid-afternoon, occasionally a fourth late-shift.
[L1458] No espresso (volume insufficient to sustain hydration). Tea on the rare days she is recovering
[L1459] from a hangover.
[L1460] Alcohol. The defining substance, behaviorally. Pattern: solo, in quarters or in a single specific
[L1461] dive bar she has used for a decade, after operationally compromising decisions. Drink of
[L1462] choice: brown liquor, neat, served in a regulation tumbler she has used long enough that the
[L1463] etching on the base has worn through. Pours are heavy and uncounted; she does not measure.
[L1464] Two to four pours on a normal bad night; five-plus on the nights she has lied to a friend.
[L1465] She does not drink in company except ceremonial (a toast at a wake) and does not drink to
[L1466] intoxication-visible-to-others. The drinking is private and is deliberately invisible to the chain of
[L1467] command, which knows about it anyway. She does not drink in the field. She does not drink
[L1468] within twelve hours of a deployment. She believes the discipline around the drinking is what
[L1469] proves the drinking is not a problem; an honest review of the volume would conclude otherwise.
[L1470] Nicotine. None. She does not smoke and never has.
[L1471] Pharmaceuticals. Ibuprofen for the body. The sleep aids she has been prescribed go unused
[L1472] — she does not trust the loss of vertical-recovery window they would require. She has refused
[L1473] on-record psychological pharmacotherapy from SHIELD medical on three documented
[L1474] occasions, citing operational fitness review concerns; the actual reason is that she will not be
[L1475] that legible.
[L1476] X. INTIMACY & SEXUAL SOMATICS
[L1477] Baseline. Effectively closed. No on-panel relationship of duration. No spouse, no partner, no
[L1478] dependents. Whether this reflects orientation, opportunity, deliberate election, or all three is
[L1479] undetermined from the record; what is determined is that she has organized her physical life so[L1480] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 47 / 206>[L1481] that intimacy is structurally inaccessible — there is no time, no residence, no off-duty self for a
[L1482] partner to know.
[L1483] Touch tolerance. Low in baseline, calibrated by trust. She does not initiate handshakes; she
[L1484] returns them firmly and briefly. Shoulder-claps from Fury are received without flinch but also
[L1485] without return. She does not hug. The few times she has been hugged (an emotional
[L1486] subordinate post-survival; Pepper Potts post-extraction) she has held still rather than
[L1487] reciprocated, hands at her sides, jaw set, until the contact ended.
[L1488] Touch she initiates. Operational only — a hand to a subordinate's shoulder to steer them
[L1489] through a door, a palm at the small of a wounded teammate's back to support weight, fingers at
[L1490] a casket lid (§III). The contact is always purposive and always brief.
[L1491] Erotic register. Inferred, sparse. The Bendis-era Stark antagonism contains a charge that both
[L1492] parties refuse to act on for years; whether it ever resolves in the published record is ambiguous
[L1493] and probably deliberately so. Whatever sexual life she conducts is conducted off-page, on her
[L1494] own terms, with strict containment from operational life. The behavioral profile predicts brief,
[L1495] infrequent, transactional contact with vetted partners — likely other operators or former
[L1496] operators — and no continuity. She would not allow someone to stay the night in a quarters she
[L1497] sleeps armed in.
[L1498] Intimacy as it actually appears. Not sexual. The closest thing to intimacy in the record is the
[L1499] two-hour bar meal with Fury, the silent ride home with Stark after the extraction, the moment
[L1500] she stood at Rogers' shoulder when no one else would — proximity, sustained, with someone
[L1501] who knows what she knows and does not require her to perform anything. This is what intimacy
[L1502] looks like for her: shared weight, no words, the body present and the guard partially down.
[L1503] XI. STATE-DEPENDENT SUMMARY MATRIX
[L1504] Calm. Posture loaded but loose. Blink rate 15/min. Breath slow. Right-corner mouth-pull
[L1505] occasionally active. Hands at belt or seam. Voice at trained register, 140 wpm.
[L1506] Cognitive load (reading a bad report, sitting through a directorate brief). Bridge gesture
[L1507] appears. Hair-tuck on the right. Jaw-clench visible. Blink rate drops to 10–12/min. Respiration
[L1508] unchanged. Voice unchanged in public, lower and quieter when alone.
[L1509] Operational stress (active op, command seat). Sentences shorten. Voice pitch flattens. Heel￾strike returns to gait as she moves the deck. Earpiece-check frequency rises. Folder-tap
[L1510] becomes more emphatic. Pupils run wide. The metronome holds.
[L1511] Threat (weapon out, hostile in close). Color leaves the face. Blink rate near zero. Right hand
[L1512] goes still on grip or table. Breath: four-in, six-out. She does not speak unless speaking is the[L1513] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 48 / 206>[L1514] tactical action. The body is fully forward of the hips and the strong-side knee is unlocked.
[L1515] Past containment / moral injury. Withdraws. The voice goes quiet rather than loud. The
[L1516] bridge gesture extends to five seconds. The drinking begins earlier in the evening. The
[L1517] knuckles take the day's weight against a bulkhead at some point before sleep.
[L1518] Genuine fear. Inhale held a beat too long. Orbital tightening. Otherwise indistinguishable from
[L1519] calm to anyone not reading at this resolution — which is the entire problem with surveilling her.
[L1520] Intimacy (the rare, slow, non-sexual kind she permits). Shoulders drop perhaps a quarter￾inch. The trained vocal register slips upward. She sits, eventually, rather than stands. She
[L1521] allows silence to be company rather than instrument. The sidearm stays on but the hand leaves
[L1522] it. Right-corner mouth-pull active and sustained. It is, on the body, the most undefended she
gets.
[L1524] End Somatic Atlas. The body in this file is a machine its operator has trained, scarred,
[L1525] medicated, and refused to retire. It tells the truth she will not say out loud, in a language only
[L1526] people who have looked this long can read.
[L1527] Attachment & Relational Patterns
[L1528] ATTACHMENT & RELATIONAL PATTERNS
[L1529] UATU dossier, Section 6. Cross-referenced against the full behavioral record from New

[L1531] 6.1 The Originating Attachment Environment
[L1532] The relational template was set in a Chicago row house before she was twelve.
[L1533] The father — never named on panel, present in Reed's 2008 one-shot as a man whose
[L1534] approval was structured as a permanent withholding — is the architect. He is not a beater; he is
[L1535] worse than that for the formation of a Maria Hill. He is a man who responds to a child's offered
[L1536] achievement with a recalibrated standard. Bring home an A and the next conversation is about
[L1537] the A+. Make varsity and the conversation is about starting. There is no terminal state of
[L1538] "enough" in his economy, because the function of "not enough" is to keep the child oriented
[L1539] toward him. The withholding is the bond.[L1540] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 49 / 206>

[52] assistant (text, 1921 chars)
Yes. That is the distinction I just violated.

The method we established was **not** “take recognizable character traits and turn them into agent personalities.” Dottie works because we mapped the **underlying functional architecture** of Maria Hill: what role that archetype occupies in a command system, how she processes information, where her authority begins and ends, how she relates to specialists, how she behaves under uncertainty, and what failure modes that particular cognitive/organizational shape counteracts. The character gives us a very dense reference model; it isn't a costume.

So with the Howling Commandos, the question isn't, “What funny Dugan behaviors should an AI have?” It's: **what does Dugan contribute to that team that the other Commandos do not, and why does a team containing all of them become more capable than the sum of its members?**

That means mapping each Commando individually—Dugan, Gabe Jones, Jim Morita, Jacques Dernier, James Montgomery Falsworth, and the rest of whichever canonical composition we're using—across the same dimensions we used for Dottie. Then we map the **interactions between those functions**. Some capabilities should overlap deliberately; some should be complementary; some should create productive opposition. Their differences should change how the system reasons, not merely how its output sounds.

And critically, **personality comes last**. If I strip every name, fictional reference, voice, catchphrase, and bit of characterization out of Aegis, I should still be able to hand you the architecture and demonstrate why six differently structured cognitive agents outperform six copies of the same general-purpose model.

Then we can put Dugan's name back on the appropriate one.

Otherwise, you're exactly right: we'd have built six chatbots in costumes holding a fucking staff meeting.

I'll stick to the established mapping methodology from here.

[L7] Executive Brief (BLUF)[L8] <IMAGE FOR PAGE: 1 / 208>[image_asset_pointer asset][L9] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 2 / 208>[L10] EXECUTIVE BRIEF (BLUF) — SUBJECT: ANTHONY
[L11] EDWARD STARK
[L12] Bottom Line, Up Front
[L13] The subject is a man who has spent sixty years apologizing, in metal, for a single
[L14] afternoon in a cave. Every other fact about him — the company, the armors, the drinking, the
[L15] women, the wars he started and the wars he ended, the Registration Act, the self-lobotomy, the
[L16] sobriety, the mentorships, the cosmic-tier refusals of late canon — is a downstream expression
[L17] of that afternoon and of the childhood that pre-loaded him to respond to it the way he did. He is
[L18] not a playboy who became a hero. He is a chronically shame-saturated, avoidantly attached,
[L19] traumatically conditioned engineer whose central life-strategy is to out-build the next
[L20] catastrophe his own mind can foresee, and whose central life-cost is that this strategy
[L21] requires him to never, under any circumstance, stop.
[L22] He is, in the deepest sense, useful. He is useful to the planet, useful to his friends, useful to the
[L23] institutions he serves and the ones he periodically destroys; he is useful to himself only insofar
[L24] as usefulness staves off the feeling that he should not exist. Remove the work and the
[L25] underlying organism is a frightened, sleep-deprived, grief-laden man with a damaged heart, a
[L26] paternal voice in his head telling him he is not enough, and a coping repertoire that has
[L27] historically defaulted to alcohol when the engineering channel jams.
[L28] The Through-Line
[L29] A single sentence carries his entire biography: the thing that protects him is the thing that
[L30] harms him, and he cannot tell the difference because they are the same thing.
[L31] The through-line is not heroism and not hubris. It is compensation. Everything visible is
[L32] compensation; the compensation is largely successful at the civilizational scale and largely
[L33] The armor protects his life and isolates him from intimacy.
[L34] His intelligence saves the world and ensures he is governed by no one slow enough to stop
[L35] him when he is wrong.
[L36] His company funds the heroes and seeded the weapons that killed Yinsen.
[L37] His sobriety is a structural achievement and a control-system that, when stressed,
[L38] substitutes self-destructive martyrdom for the bottle without changing the underlying affect it
[L39] is suppressing.
[L40] His foresight is genuine — he is usually right early — and his foresight is the engine of
[L41] every unilateral overreach in his record.
[L42] His father damaged him and his father is the template he cannot stop iterating; the late￾canon mentorship of Riri Williams, Peter Parker, and others is the cleanest reparative act of
[L43] his life precisely because it is the inversion of Howard.[L44] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 3 / 208>[L45] unsuccessful at the personal one.
[L46] The Core Wound
[L47] The core wound is not the cave. The cave is the activating trauma; the wound it activated was
[L48] already there.
[L49] The core wound is the conditioned belief, laid down in childhood by Howard Stark's cold
[L50] comparative criticism and Maria Stark's warm unavailability, that he is loved
[L51] conditionally and only for what he produces — and that even maximum production will be
[L52] measured against an absent ideal (Captain America, in Howard's case; later, Stark's own
[L53] internalized impossible standard) and found insufficient. The cave then supplied a second,
[L54] catastrophically congruent lesson: that the things you build, if you are not vigilant enough, will
[L55] be used to kill people who trusted you. The two lessons fuse. The resulting operating belief —
[L56] never stated to himself in these words but visible in every decision — is:
[L57] I am responsible for everything my mind creates. My mind creates dangerous things.
[L58] Therefore I must control everything. And I will fail.
[L59] This is unlivable as a belief and undefeatable as a motivator. It is the engine of his greatness
[L60] and the source of every meaningful injury he has caused himself and others.
[L61] Maintenance of the Wound
[L62] The wound is maintained by a tightly integrated system of behaviors that each appear adaptive
[L63] in isolation and that together guarantee the wound never closes:
[L64] 1. Workshop retreat as affect regulation. Unstructured time is intolerable; the workbench
[L65] reliably down-regulates anxiety; therefore there is no unstructured time in which the
[L66] underlying affect could be felt, named, or metabolized. The defense works perfectly and
[L67] prevents recovery permanently.
[L68] 2. Concealment-from-intimates framed as protection. He hides medical facts, mission risk,
[L69] and emotional state from Pepper, Rhodey, and others on the rationale that disclosure would
[L70] burden them. The rationale is sincere and is also a mechanism by which he ensures no one
[L71] ever sees him whole, which is what he most fears and most needs.
[L72] 3. Compensatory grandiosity under shame load. The "genius, billionaire, philanthropist"
[L73] performance reliably activates at the moments his shame is most acute. This convinces
[L74] audiences (and casual diagnosticians) that the grandiosity is primary. It is not. It is a shame￾management device, which is why it is brittle and why it collapses into self-flagellation on
[L75] contact with a peer who refuses to be impressed.
[L76] 4. Identification of self with hardware. The decades-long migration of the armor from a suit￾in-a-suitcase, to under-skin nanotech, to neural integration, to AI-substrate reconstitution, is
[L77] the somatic signature of the wound: the patient is collapsing the distance between Tony[L78] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 4 / 208>[L79] These seven maintenance mechanisms are mutually reinforcing. Disrupting any one of them
[L80] threatens the others, which is why he resists disruption with the full force of his intelligence and
[L81] why his episodes of genuine growth (post-Bottle Bethany/Jarvis scaffolding; the homeless-arc
[L82] recovery; the Cantwell-era explicit recovery program; the Carol-as-sponsor relationships of late
[L83] canon) have all required external relational scaffolding plus a tractable engineering
[L84] problem in parallel — pure insight, pure rest, and pure surrender have all historically failed
[L85] with him.
[L86] What He Is, Underneath
[L87] Strip the armor, the company, the press, the suits and the suits-in-the-suits, and the organism
[L88] that remains is:
[L89] Stark and Iron Man because that distance is the place where he feels he can be killed,
[L90] abandoned, or proven insufficient.
[L91] 5. Sobriety-as-control-system rather than sobriety-as-surrender. His abstinence is real
[L92] and durable but it is held the way he holds everything: by engineering. When the
[L93] engineering of sobriety is stressed past its limits, the underlying affect does not get felt; it
[L94] gets routed into martyrdom (self-erasure in Disassembled, the willingness to die in late￾canon cosmic confrontations) which is a sober relapse — a different vehicle for the same
[L95] impulse to make the unbearable feeling stop.
[L96] 6. Catastrophe-foresight as moral mandate. Because he can see further than the room, he
[L97] believes he is obligated to act further than the room. This converts every accurate prediction
[L98] into a license for unilateralism (Registration, the Illuminati, Armor Wars), which generates
[L99] new harms, which generate new shame, which feed the wound.
[L100] 7. Intimacy short-cycling. Pursuit → idealization → engineered exit at the moment of
[L101] sustained intimacy demand. The pattern repeats across Janice Cord, Bethany Cabe,
[L102] Rumiko Fujikawa, Maya Hansen, and the recurrent Pepper cycle. He cannot accept being
[L103] loved without performance because his original template did not permit it; the relationships
[L104] end before the template can be disconfirmed.
[L105] A man with a chronic, mortality-salient cardiac condition who has lived for six decades
[L106] knowing his heart will stop without a device he engineered.
[L107] A man whose interoception is poor, whose sleep is curtailed by choice, whose nervous
[L108] system has been rewritten and rebuilt enough times that baseline cannot be cleanly
[L109] defined.
[L110] A man with intact, even acute empathy, which is the reason the shame is as severe as it is
[L111] — he feels the harms his work causes with full fidelity and has nowhere to put the feeling.
[L112] A man whose humor is genuine, whose loyalty is deep within a very small circle (Rhodey is
[L113] the most stable relationship of his life, longer-running and less ambivalent than any[L114] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 5 / 208>[L115] Operational Summary
[L116] Functional capacity: elite, sustained, civilization-scale. Among the most capable individuals on
[L117] the planet across engineering, executive, combat, and strategic-foresight domains. Capacity
[L118] does not degrade gracefully under stress; it intensifies until catastrophic failure.
[L119] Reliability: high on task, conditional on relationship. Will keep a promise to a stranger more
[L120] reliably than a promise to an intimate, because the intimate triggers the avoidance architecture.
[L121] Predictability under stress (escalation curve): mild stress → more work, less sleep, more
[L122] flirtation; moderate stress → secrecy and unilateral contingency planning; severe stress →
[L123] omnipotent-control behaviors at institutional scale; decompensation → historically alcohol,
[L124] currently self-destructive martyrdom. The curve is stable across sixty years of record and
[L125] across writers; the vehicle of decompensation has changed, the trajectory has not.
[L126] Manipulability: low through coercion, low through flattery (he sees both), moderate through
[L127] appeals to responsibility (his shame is a lever and a sophisticated adversary — Stane, Osborn,
[L128] Doom in various eras — has used it), high through threats to people he loves, near-total
[L129] through the demonstration that his technology has harmed someone. Anyone who can credibly
[L130] show him a child injured by a Stark-derived weapon owns him for the duration of the
[L131] conversation.
[L132] Containment: he is not containable by institutions; he is containable only by relationships. The
[L133] historical containment set is small and specific: Rhodey (loyalty floor, willingness to wear the
[L134] armor and to take it off him), Pepper (the only voice he reliably hears say no), Steve Rogers
[L135] when the relationship is intact (peer moral authority of a kind Howard withheld), Carol Danvers
[L136] in recent canon (sponsor-coded direct confrontation), and the memory of Yinsen (which he
[L137] carries as a permanent internal object and which has prevented at least as many bad decisions
[L138] as it has caused). Remove this set and there is no governor on the system.
[L139] Risk profile: the dominant risks are not external. They are (a) relapse under accumulated
[L140] stress, (b) self-sacrificial decision-making framed as utilitarian necessity, (c) unilateral
[L141] romantic attachment), and whose capacity for apology and reversal is real (post-Civil-War,
[L142] post-Inversion, post-Incursion).
[L143] A man whose mentorship of younger inheritors is the cleanest, least defended channel he
[L144] has, because it permits him to give what he could not receive without requiring him to
[L145] receive in return.
[L146] A man who is, in late canon, doing the actual work — naming defects out loud, sponsoring
[L147] others, refusing offered power — and who is therefore more dangerous to himself than ever,
[L148] because the maintenance mechanisms above are still online and the new healthier
[L149] defenses (conscious recovery, suspicion of grandiosity) are themselves capable of being
[L150] weaponized into another, subtler control-system.[L151] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 6 / 208>[L152] planetary-scale intervention justified by accurate foresight, and (d) the slow corrosion of
[L153] intimate relationships through protective concealment. External adversaries have never come
[L154] close to ending him; he has come close to ending himself, in one form or another,
[L155] approximately once a decade for six decades.
[L156] Trajectory: improving, fragilely. The late-canon work is real. The wound is not closed and will
[L157] not close; the relationship to the wound is, for the first time in the record, conscious. This is the
[L158] most that can be asked of him and it is more than was visible at any earlier point.
[L159] The One-Line File
[L160] A brilliant, frightened, decent man who built a metal heart to keep a wounded one
[L161] beating, and then spent the rest of his life making sure the metal one never failed anyone
[L162] the way he believes the wounded one failed Yinsen.
[L163] Chronology I — Origin & Childhood
[L164] CHRONOLOGY I — ORIGIN & CHILDHOOD
[L165] Anthony Edward Stark, b. 29 May (the canonical date used
[L166] across Marvel reference works since the Official Handbook
[L167] era); Long Island, New York. The ground floor.
[L168] 1. The House Before the Child
[L169] To understand the subject one must first map the household into which he was decanted,
[L170] because Tony Stark was not raised so much as he was engineered as collateral output of an
[L171] industrial enterprise that pre-existed him by a generation.
[L172] Howard Anthony Walter Stark (b. circa 1917 in canonical references; introduced retroactively
[L173] in Iron Man #28, 1970, and substantially fleshed out across Iron Man: The Iron Age #1–2 by
[L174] Kurt Busiek, 1998; the Bendis/Maleev flashbacks in New Avengers: Illuminati and Avengers
[L175] Prime; the Brubaker/Epting Winter Soldier reveal in Captain America vol. 5; the Original Sin:
[L176] Hulk vs. Iron Man arc by Waid/Kindt, 2014; and Dan Slott's Invincible Iron Man (2022–)
[L177] reframings). Howard is depicted with extraordinary consistency across writers: brilliant engineer,
[L178] defense contractor to the OSS and then to SHIELD's precursor apparatus; a man whose
[L179] closest emotional relationships were with Abraham Erskine (briefly), with the unconscious body
[L180] of Steve Rogers (whom he searched for in the Arctic across the postwar decades, often
[L181] returning home to his small son drunk and obsessed with another man), and with Jarvis the
[L182] butler — never with his wife and never with his son. Howard's mode is demonstration: he built,[L183] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 7 / 208>[L184] drank, traveled, performed his greatness for boardrooms, and treated paternity as an
[L185] organizational chart on which Tony was the next appointment.
[L186] Maria Collins Carbonell Stark (introduced in passing in the original Lee/Heck run; consistently
[L187] developed from the 1990s forward; substantially expanded in the Iron Man (1998) Busiek run, in
[L188] Iron Man: Season One by Howard Chaykin (2012), and in the Original Sin tie-ins). Maria is
[L189] rendered as the warmer parent and is also — and this is the key structural fact — the less
[L190] present parent, in a way that is not really her fault: she is the wife of Howard Stark, which is a
[L191] full occupation. She plays piano (an important detail to which the canon returns repeatedly: Iron
[L192] Man (Fraction) #500, the Cantwell run, the Hickman Avengers flashbacks all reference her at
[L193] the keys), speaks several languages, came from old Italian-American money on the Carbonell
[L194] side, and serves as the household's emotional translator. Her warmth toward Tony is real and is
[L195] also conditional on its not embarrassing Howard.
[L196] The Original Sin arc and the Slott (2022– ) run together establish a third structurally critical fact:
[L197] Tony is adopted, or at least his biological provenance is contested in canon. The Slott reveal
[L198] — that Tony is the biological son of Amanda Armstrong (a SHIELD operative) and Jude — was
[L199] published in 2014's Iron Man #19–28 (Gillen, The Secret Origin of Tony Stark) and elaborated
[L200] in Iron Man (2020) Cantwell and in 2022's Slott run. Arno Stark is, depending on the era, either
[L201] a fabricated brother, a true brother, or a parallel-future variant. For this section's purposes the
[L202] functional truth matters more than the genetic one: the child raised in the Stark house was
[L203] raised under the belief that he was Howard and Maria's son and under the lived experience of
[L204] being Howard's heir-apparent, and that is what shaped him. The adoption datum becomes
[L205] psychologically operative only retroactively, in adulthood, when it lands as a retroactive
[L206] confirmation of a feeling he had carried for sixty years — I never quite belonged in that house
[L207] — and produces no integration crisis precisely because it changes nothing about what already
[L208] happened to him.
[L209] Edwin Jarvis (introduced Tales of Suspense #59, 1964, originally as Avengers Mansion butler;
[L210] established as a Stark household fixture from childhood onward across multiple retcons).
[L211] Functionally the child's primary caregiver. The man who fed him, dressed him, sat outside his
[L212] door when he had nightmares, kept the bourbon decanters topped up so Howard would not
[L213] notice anyone had been at them, and — most importantly — was the only adult in the house
[L214] who used the boy's name as a name rather than as a designation of inheritance. Tony's later
[L215] capacity for warmth toward staff, his consistent first-name basis with everyone from Happy
[L216] Hogan to junior assistants, his AI's name in the modernized canon — all of this is Jarvis￾loading.
[L217] 2. Birth and Infancy[L218] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 8 / 208>[L219] Born on Long Island; the specific Stark estate (subsequently variously located in Oyster Bay,
[L220] Southampton, and "the North Shore" depending on writer) is established as the primary
[L221] residence through the boarding-school years. The birth itself is depicted in the Iron Age and
[L222] Season One flashbacks as a Howard-absent event — he is in Washington, or in Los Alamos, or
[L223] "in the field" — and Maria recovers with staff. Tony is named after his maternal great￾grandfather Anthony Carbonell (per the Busiek-era genealogy) and given Howard's middle
[L224] name as a middle name — Anthony Edward — a small concession that nonetheless inscribes
[L225] the father into the body of the boy.
[L226] Infancy is materially privileged and emotionally unstaffed. The household runs a roster of
[L227] nurses; Maria is involved but episodically; Howard appears at intervals. The earliest
[L228] documented behavioral note (Busiek, Iron Age) is that Tony does not cry for attention as an
[L229] infant — he is described as quiet, watchful, "an unsettlingly observant baby." Whether this is
[L230] the writer's romanticism or a clinically meaningful early temperamental finding, it is consistent
[L231] with the adult presentation: high baseline arousal, externally calm presentation, dense
[L232] observational uptake.
[L233] 3. Toddlerhood and the Workshop
[L234] The single most documented and most psychologically loaded childhood scene in the entire
[L235] Stark canon is the workshop. Across every era of telling — from the original Stan Lee
[L236] thumbnail through Iron Age, Season One, the Fraction run, the Slott run, and the film-canon
[L237] flashbacks of Iron Man 2 — Howard's workshop appears as the primary venue of father–son
[L238] contact, and the circuit board appears as the medium of love.
[L239] Canon establishes that Tony built a functioning circuit board at four (originally Stan Lee,
[L240] reaffirmed across every subsequent biography), built a working V8 engine at six (Iron Age and
[L241] consistent across retellings), and produced his first true patent-quality engineering work —
[L242] variously a transistor refinement, a miniaturization breakthrough, or a structural-alloy
[L243] modification — before the age of ten. These accomplishments are not artifacts of natural
[L244] childhood play; they are audition tapes for Howard. The behavioral pattern visible from age four
[L245] onward is: child observes father's preoccupation → child manufactures object likely to interest
[L246] father → child presents object → father responds with assessment rather than affection → child
[L247] internalizes that assessment is the form love takes in this house → child returns to bench to
[L248] make a better object. The pattern, repeated thousands of times over a decade, becomes the
[L249] foundational neural circuit for adult Stark's entire mode of relating: produce, present, be
[L250] evaluated, iterate. It is also the foundational substrate for the workshop-as-anxiolytic that will
[L251] dominate his adult life.
[L252] There are two recurrent micro-scenes in the canon worth flagging at granular resolution:[L253] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 9 / 208>[L254] 4. Maria, the Piano, and the Italian Side
[L255] Maria's piano is canonically a Steinway grand in the east drawing room (Cantwell-era depiction;
[L256] consistent in flashback panels going back to the 1970s). The child sits under it while she plays.
[L257] This is the only documented setting in which Tony Stark, child or adult, is shown in
[L258] uncomplicated passive enjoyment of another person's presence — no production demand,
[L259] no evaluation, just acoustic envelopment. The adult correlate is observable: Stark's
[L260] documented preference for classic rock and AC/DC notwithstanding, he plays piano
[L261] competently himself in several runs (Fraction #500; Cantwell), and the only music canonically
[L262] shown to reliably calm him during panic states is solo piano. Maria taught him. He never tells
[L263] anyone this.
[L264] Maria's Italian family — the Carbonells of New York via Naples — provides his only sustained
[L265] early exposure to unembarrassed warmth and physical demonstrativeness. Summer visits
[L266] to Maria's relatives are depicted (briefly, in Iron Age and in Gillen's Secret Origin) as the
[L267] chronological pockets in which the child laughs without strategy. They are also where he first
[L268] encounters the cultural fact that men can embrace other men without it being a defect, a datum
[L269] he does not consciously integrate but which surfaces, decades later, in the unselfconscious
[L270] physical warmth he shows to Rhodey and (pre-Civil-War) to Steve.
[L271] Maria is also the first person to drink in front of him in a controlled, social, non￾pathological way — wine at dinner, prosecco at the Carbonell holidays — and this matters: his
[L272] earliest model of alcohol is not Howard's bourbon-and-secrets but Maria's table wine. This is
[L273] the model he later destroys.
[L274] 5. The Boarding-School Exile
[L275] Howard's hand on the back of the child's neck while the child solders. Depicted in Iron
[L276] Age and recurrent in dream-imagery in the Fraction and Cantwell runs. The gesture is the
[L277] closest Howard comes to physical tenderness — a guiding, slightly too-firm pressure that is
[L278] half affection and half correction. The adult Stark will flinch, observably, when touched on
[L279] the back of the neck unexpectedly (a tell visible in several New Avengers and Bendis-era
[L280] panels where it is rendered as quick irritation; the body remembers).
[L281] The interrupted question. Across multiple flashbacks the child asks Howard something —
[L282] about a schematic, about Captain America, about why mother is crying — and Howard
[L283] answers a different, technically adjacent question, redirecting from affect to engineering.
[L284] The adult Stark does this to others compulsively. He learned the move at the bench.[L285] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 10 / 208>[L286] Tony is sent to boarding school early — variously rendered as age seven (the early canon,
[L287] harsh), age nine (Busiek normalization), or age eleven (Cantwell softening) — at an unnamed
[L288] New England prep institution that across writers reads as a composite of Choate, Phillips
[L289] Andover, and Lawrenceville. The decision is Howard's; Maria opposes it ineffectually. The
[L290] stated rationale is he needs to be challenged. The functional effect is abandonment dressed
[L291] as opportunity.
[L292] Behavioral consequences observable in the surviving childhood record:
[L293] The boarding-school years also produce his first sustained peer attachments: shifting cohorts of
[L294] older, often wealthier, often more dissolute classmates who teach him to perform a version of
[L295] playboy heir that will become a lifelong mask. He learns at fifteen how to hold a room of forty￾year-olds at a Stark Industries gala. He does not learn how to hold a conversation with his own
[L296] mother.
[L297] 6. MIT and the Compressed Adolescence
[L298] Admitted to MIT at fifteen (canonical across every era; the single most stable biographical
[L299] datum after the cave). Graduate-level work by seventeen; dual master's in electrical
[L300] engineering and physics by nineteen (Busiek-era settlement of the credentials, broadly
[L301] maintained).
[L302] He skips two grades within the first year, then a third (placing him roughly three years
[L303] younger than peers for the remainder of secondary schooling — a structural source of
[L304] social isolation that compounds the affective isolation).
[L305] He becomes the class clown by deliberate construction — the documented genesis of
[L306] the adult quip-defense. Verbal speed becomes the tool by which he prevents older boys
[L307] from bullying him for being small, young, and rich; it becomes the tool by which he secures
[L308] attention from teachers; it becomes, over years, the only register in which he reliably knows
[L309] how to be liked.
[L310] He develops the first iteration of the workshop-as-sanctuary pattern at school, colonizing
[L311] first the science lab and then a literal closet adjacent to it as private workspace. School
[L312] records (per Iron Age) note he is found sleeping there more nights than in his dormitory bed.
[L313] He acquires his first taste of alcohol on school grounds, at approximately thirteen (Busiek;
[L314] reaffirmed elsewhere). Stolen from a master's office. He is alone when he drinks it. He
[L315] notes — and the writers, across decades, are careful to inscribe this — that it stops the
[L316] feeling in his chest. That sentence, in various phrasings, recurs as the originary alcohol
[L317] memory across the entire publication history. He has the AUD substrate before he ever has
[L318] the trauma; the trauma activates a system that is already loaded.[L319] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 11 / 208>[L320] MIT is where the adult personality structure crystallizes:
[L321] 7. The Parental Death
[L322] The car crash on Long Island, approximately Tony's late teens (variously seventeen, nineteen,
[L323] twenty-one across retellings; settled by Brubaker's Winter Soldier reveal as occurring in 1991-
[L324] equivalent in modernized timeline, though the comics' sliding-time means the year keeps
[L325] moving). Both parents killed. Originally rendered as straightforward accident; retconned
[L326] definitively by Brubaker as Hydra-ordered assassination executed by the Winter Soldier (Bucky
[L327] Barnes), with the rationale that Howard had developed a serum or weapon Hydra wanted
[L328] intercepted.
[L329] The psychological loading of this event has three discrete layers:
[L330] First real friendship — James Rhodes. Met at MIT in the original telling; in later canon
[L331] shifted slightly to the Air Force ROTC overlap or to a post-graduate context. Rhodey is
[L332] older, militarily disciplined, Black, working-class, and immune to Stark money in a way Tony
[L333] has never previously encountered in a peer. The relationship is the first in which Stark
[L334] experiences being liked for being annoying rather than despite it — Rhodey gives him grief
[L335] and stays. This becomes the template for every friendship he will subsequently keep. The
[L336] fact that he keeps very few is partly because the template is rare.
[L337] First documented heavy drinking. Per Iron Age and reaffirmed in the Fraction run, MIT is
[L338] where the school-grounds sips become a routine. He functions; the grades do not slip; the
[L339] feeling in the chest recedes more reliably. The functional alcoholic phenotype is in place
[L340] before he is twenty.
[L341] First sustained sexual pattern. Compulsive, charming, brief. Established at MIT and
[L342] unchanged for forty subsequent years of canon.
[L343] First documented panic episode, retroactively rendered in the Cantwell run: a freshman￾year incident in a crowded lecture hall, attributed by the boy to "bad lunch," recognizable to
[L344] a clinician as a panic attack. He does not tell anyone. He goes back to the bench.
[L345] 1. The original loss. The last conversation with Howard is, across every retelling, unresolved.
[L346] The boy and the father were mid-argument, or mid-distance, or mid-silence. There is no
[L347] scene of reconciliation in the canon, ever, between living Tony and living Howard. Every
[L348] reconciliation occurs through artifacts — recovered film reels (Iron Man 2 analog scenes
[L349] have comics correlates), notebooks, letters Howard left in vaults, posthumous holograms.
[L350] The father–son relationship is conducted, in its entirety, posthumously. This is structurally
[L351] devastating and also, perversely, manageable: dead Howard can be edited; living Howard
[L352] could not be reached.[L353] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 12 / 208>[L354] He inherits the company at majority. He inherits, with it, Obadiah Stane as acting CEO and
[L355] trusted family advisor — the man who has been waiting two decades to gut him. He does not
[L356] see it coming. He is twenty-one and drunk and the smartest person in every room and he does
[L357] not see it coming because he is busy being the smartest person in every room.
[L358] 8. The Earliest Behavioral Patterns — Substantiated Synthesis
[L359] By the close of childhood (drawing the line at the parental deaths, before the cave), the
[L360] following patterns are demonstrably already installed and will not meaningfully change for sixty
[L361] years of subsequent canon:
[L362] 2. The Maria loss. Less elaborated in canon, more devastating in inference. The piano falls
[L363] silent. The only person in the house whose love did not require demonstration is gone. The
[L364] adult Stark's capacity for receiving uncomplicated affection — as distinct from his capacity
[L365] to perform charm in order to elicit affection — dies on Long Island at the same intersection.
[L366] 3. The retroactive Winter Soldier loading. When this datum surfaces in adult Stark's
[L367] consciousness (Original Sin; film-canon Civil War analog material has comics resonances in
[L368] the Bendis post-Original Sin runs), it produces the catastrophic rupture with Steve Rogers
[L369] — but it also confirms a suspicion the patient has carried his whole life: the world is rigged;
[L370] the systems that look accidental are actually designed; my pain has authors. This converts
[L371] grief into a paranoid epistemology that thereafter shapes every governance instinct he has.
[L372] Production as the language of love. Installed at the workshop bench, age four. Every
[L373] adult act of invention is, at some level, a circuit board presented to a dead father.
[L374] Verbal speed as social armor. Installed at boarding school, age seven-to-eleven. The quip
[L375] is older than the suit.
[L376] Workshop as sanctuary from affect. Installed at boarding school. The cave does not
[L377] create this pattern; the cave activates it at industrial scale.
[L378] Alcohol as chest-feeling regulator. Installed at thirteen. The Dvorak coping-motives
[L379] architecture (cited in the workup) is mapped onto an already coping-motivated drinker by
[L380] the time trauma arrives.
[L381] Charm-forward, disclosure-avoidant intimacy. Installed across the MIT years, modeled
[L382] on Howard's public-private split and on the playboy-heir performance learned at galas.
[L383] Anticipatory catastrophizing about systems failure. Installed by watching Howard's
[L384] defense work and by the chronic background hum of a household in which something
[L385] important might go wrong at any moment and father will be furious. The Cassandra problem
[L386] begins as filial hypervigilance.
[L387] Atonement as identity. Installed by Howard's withholding. The child who cannot earn
[L388] enough approval to satisfy the father becomes the adult who cannot build enough safety to[L389] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 13 / 208>[L390] The cave will not make this man. The cave will reveal him to himself. The ground floor is
[L391] already poured by the time he gets on the plane to Afghanistan, and every subsequent structure
[L392] he builds — the armor, the company, the Registry, the Bunker, the Illuminati, the sobriety, the
[L393] recovery — rests on a foundation laid by a four-year-old at a workbench, soldering a circuit
[L394] board, waiting for a man who was not coming back from the war to look up and notice him.

[L400] 2.1 The Late Adolescence — Boarding School, MIT, and the
[L401] Architecture of the Inner Life
[L402] The subject is placed in boarding school early. Canonical references across the
[L403] Michelinie/Layton runs, the Kurt Busiek Iron Man: The Iron Age miniseries, and the
[L404] Bendis/Maleev flashbacks in International Iron Man converge on Phillips Academy or an
[L405] analogue from roughly age 11–13. The placement is not a punishment; it is, in the parental
[L406] ledger, a resource allocation. Howard does not have time. Maria does not have the standing to
[L407] override Howard. The boy is moved to a place where the staff is paid to manage him.
[L408] Behavioral data from this period (extractable from in-canon flashback, second-hand testimony
[L409] from Jarvis, and the patient's own intoxicated disclosures in later years):
[L410] satisfy the world.
[L411] Asymmetric mentorship as the cleanest available intimacy. Modeled by Jarvis.
[L412] Reproduced, eventually, with Peter Parker, Riri Williams, Amadeus Cho — every one of
[L413] them a chance to be the adult he needed and did not have.
[L414] Academic performance. Off the top of the curve in mathematics, physics, and the proto￾computer-science of the period. Indifferent-to-resentful in humanities subjects he later, as
[L415] an adult, became autodidactically formidable in (history of philosophy, classical music,
[L416] Renaissance metallurgy — the gaps were defensive, not innate).
[L417] Social pattern. Two reliable modes: (a) court jester for older boys (the proto-form of the
[L418] press-conference persona — buy attention with wit, deflect intimacy with self-mockery); (b)
[L419] solitary, in the machine shop or the library, for the bulk of unstructured hours. He had[L420] <PARSED TEXT FOR PAGE: 14 / 208>[L421] By 15 he is at MIT — by every account the youngest in his cohort by a significant margin,
[L422] isolated by both intellect and chronology. He completes two doctorates (electrical engineering
[L423] and physics in the standard tellings, with a third — applied mathematics — sometimes added)
[L424] by age 19. The relevant pattern, which a surveillance file would note coldly:
[L425] Subject's entire structured life from age 13 to age 19 is a sequence of accelerated mastery
[L426] of nested technical systems. No sustained romantic relationship. No team-sport
[L427] participation. No religious affiliation. No therapeutic contact. No spiritual practice. Affect
[L428] regulation is single-channel and chemical.
[L429] He meets James Rhodes in this period in some tellings and in the Vietnam-era cave in others;
[L430] the canonical present-day reconciliation treats the friendship as predating the captivity, with
[L431] Rhodey already serving as the first person the subject permits to talk to him without buying
[L432] anything from him. The significance of this datum cannot be overstated. Rhodey is the first

File
[L436] The car crash that kills Howard and Maria occurs in the subject's late teens (variably ages 17–

[L460] deterrence, "if not us, then someone less responsible" — are the standard ones in the industry;
